dev.tanrei.vocabulary.rationale: One product shows compact choices, suggested actions and entered items as small labelled controls, in rows on a plain surface and over media, at two densities, some of them on or off, some of them removable — where removing loses something and where it does not — enabled and disabled.

dev.tanrei.llm.usage: Everything a chip reads: per size its height, paddings, gap, label text style, icon, avatar and remove-target sizes; its corner (a pill in the default system), outline width and the shapes of its avatar and remove target; and per variant (outlined, elevated) the colors and elevation of a chip (container, outline, label, leading icon, remove action), of a remove action that reads as destructive (destructive-remove.), and of a selected filter chip (selected.), in each state.
rules: kind decides what a chip does: action (a button), filter (on or off), input (an entered item the user can remove). The variant only decides how it looks.
Use elevated only where chips sit over media or a busy background; outlined everywhere else.
A filter chip that is on shows a check and the selected look; do not make selected look like unselected.
Always give an input chip a removeLabel (the remove action's accessible name).
The chip does not manage a row of chips: arrow keys, selection across chips, wrapping and moving focus after a removal belong to the layout that holds them.

state-layer.color, selected.state-layer.color, remove.state-layer.color and destructive-remove.state-layer.color are the colors hover, focus and press mix into the chip's container, a selected chip's container and the remove action's round container.

The remove action reads as destructive only while destructiveRemove is set: destructive-remove. parts rest at the remove. values and take the error color only while the remove action is hovered, focused or pressed. Set it where removing loses something that cannot be put back in a step. Never rely on the color alone: removeLabel names the action.
Heights are minimums: a height must hold 2 × padding-block + one label line, and the build reports it when it does not.

An input chip's remove action sits concentric with the chip's round end: container.padding-inline-with-remove is (height − icon) / 2 at each size. A layer that changes a chip's height, its icon size or its remove target keeps that relation, or pins the padding it wants.

shape.$description: The corner of the container, capped at half its height: sys.shape.corner.full makes the chip a pill at any height.

padding-inline.$description: Padding at an end where the label meets the edge.

padding-inline-with-icon.$description: Padding at an end that holds a glyph with no round shape of its own behind it (the leading icon, or the check of a selected filter chip); tighter than the label's, so the glyph optically aligns. The end that holds the remove action has its own padding (padding-inline-with-remove).

padding-inline-with-avatar.$description: Padding at the start when an avatar is present: a round image sits closer to the edge than a glyph. Equal to (height − avatar) / 2 at each size, so the avatar is concentric with a pill's round end.

padding-inline-with-remove.$description: Padding at the end that holds an input chip's remove glyph. Equal to (height − icon) / 2 at each size (medium (32 − 24) / 2 = 4, small (24 − 20) / 2 = 2), so the glyph's center is the center of a pill's round end and the remove action's round container, which is centered on the glyph, is inset from the end by what it is inset from the top and the bottom: (height − remove.container.size) / 2, 2 at medium and 0 at small.

dev.tanrei.vocabulary.rationale: One product pads the end that holds a round remove action apart from an end that holds a bare glyph: the remove action has a round shape of its own that shows on hover, focus and press, and that shape has to sit concentric with the chip's end, as an avatar does at the other end; a bare icon has no shape to align and is placed by eye.

padding-block.$description: Vertical padding around the row's tallest item (the label's line or a glyph's box). Heights are minimums, so this only shows when text is enlarged. Small is 2 so that its 20 glyph fits the 24 height: 20 + 2 × 2 = 24.

gap.$description: Distance between the leading icon or avatar and the label, and between the label and the remove action.

size.$description: The box of the leading icon, the check and the remove glyph, per size: the largest step of sys.icon that fits the height with the block padding (small 20 + 2 × 2 = 24; medium 24 + 2 × 4 = 32).

dev.tanrei.derive.fixed: Material 3 draws chip icons at 18dp, between Tanrei's icon steps.

weight.$description: The weight a selected filter chip's check is drawn at (the `wght` axis of the icon font): the system's weight for a control's own mark, as the checkbox draws its own, because the check is drawn on the chip's selected fill only while it is on and is what tells on from off beside the fill's color. The check's box (icon.size) does not change with it; only the stroke does. The leading icon and the remove glyph keep sys.icon.weight.

dev.tanrei.vocabulary.rationale: One product needs the check of a filter chip that is on seen at a glance at the weight its checkboxes draw theirs, since at 20 or 24 a light stroke reads fainter than its color; a product with dense filter rows draws it lighter without touching its icons.

size.$description: The side of an input chip's avatar, per size.

The side of the round shape behind the remove glyph that shows its own hover, focus and press: the glyph's box and 2 on each side, so the state layer shows as a ring around the filled glyph, and never taller than the chip (small 20 + 4 = 24, the chip's height; medium 24 + 4 = 28). It takes no part in the layout; it is centered on the glyph, which container.padding-inline-with-remove places so that this shape is concentric with the chip's round end. The hit area is larger (see the spec).

dev.tanrei.derive.fixed: This variant has no fill; the surface behind shows through.

color.$description: The edge of an outlined chip at rest. In the default system it is the hairline role, the color the divider draws its line in. It keeps its own token so that a system can draw the edge apart from its dividers.
The color hover, focus and press mix into the container: the label color.

dev.tanrei.derive.fixed: The remove action draws no fill at rest; hover, focus and press show on it.

color.$description: The color hover, focus and press of the remove action mix into its own round container.

dev.tanrei.derive.fixed: The remove action draws no fill at rest; hover, focus and press show on it.

color.$description: At rest a destructive remove glyph looks like any other; the default system turns it sys.color.error while it is hovered, focused or pressed (a rule).
The color hover, focus and press of a destructive remove action mix into its round container: the error role.

dev.tanrei.derive.fixed: A selected chip is told by its fill; it has no border.

elevation.$description: The elevated chip's resting depth. Tanrei's level1 is only the hairline ring, which draws the same edge as the outlined chip, so it rests at level2; a system whose level1 is a real shadow (m3-like, cupertino) sets level1.

The color hover, focus and press of a destructive remove action mix into its round container: the error role.

elevation.$description: As the elevated chip's resting depth: level2 here, level1 in a system whose level1 is a real shadow.

state-duration.$description: How long a change of state takes. It follows the size (small over the compact role, medium over the default role): a smaller control changes state sooner.

feedback-duration.$description: How long the answer to a press takes to spread when sys.behavior.pressed-feedback is ripple (as Button's).

selection-duration.$description: How long a filter chip takes to show or hide its check (the chip's width changes with it) and to change to or from the selected look.
